zh_alt: 示意圖：停經後出血的兩個方向、超音波的位置，以及什麼情況要取到組織。第一段是兩個方向的機率，來自同一份統合分析（Clarke 2018：129 篇研究、34,432 位停經後出血女性、6,358 位內膜癌病人，合計 40,790 人）。從癌回推症狀：內膜癌的病人裡有停經後出血這個表現的佔 91%，95% 信賴區間 87% 到 93%，不分期別。從症狀回推癌：停經後出血的女性裡最後診斷為內膜癌的佔 9%，95% 信賴區間 8% 到 11%。這個 9% 會隨族群移動：依有沒有使用荷爾蒙治療，在 7%（6 到 9%）與 12%（9 到 15%）之間，異質性 p 小於 0.001；依地區，北美 5%（3 到 11%）、西歐 13%（9 到 19%），p 等於 0.09。圖上並註明這是「已經因為出血來看病」的族群的分母，不是全人口的風險。第二段畫超音波的位置，並在圖上寫明：這張圖沒有一條「厚度正常就回家觀察」的箭頭，超音波在這裡只有一個角色，就是幫忙決定今天要不要就取到組織、要不要直接排子宮鏡。這一段有三格，必須同框讀。第一格是閾值能做到什麼：以 5 毫米為閾值，敏感度 96.2%（92.3 到 98.1）、特異度只有 51.5%（42.3 到 60.7），分母是 44 篇、17,339 位停經後出血女性、1,341 例內膜癌（7.7%）；特異度會被荷爾蒙拉低，沒有使用荷爾蒙者 92%（90 到 94%），使用中者掉到 77%（75 到 79%），分母是 35 篇、5,892 人；以個別病人資料重算，整體判別力 AUC 只有 0.82 到 0.84，作者寫過去的統合分析可能高估了它的診斷準確度，並建議排除用的閾值降到 3 毫米。第二格是指引原文：美國婦產科醫學會 2018 年第 734 號委員會意見寫，內膜厚度 4 毫米以下對內膜癌有超過 99% 的陰性預測值；同一份文件也寫，經陰道超音波不是沒有出血的停經後女性的篩檢工具，偶然發現內膜大於 4 毫米但沒有出血的人不需要例行進一步檢查。第三格是它在誰身上會漏掉，畫成四條偽陰性機率的長條（Doll 2024，1,494 人、210 例內膜癌，單一族群的黑人女性研究）：內膜厚度小於 5 毫米在停經後出血次族群的偽陰性機率 12.4%（95% CI 7.8 到 18.5）、全世代 11.4%（210 例中漏掉 24 例）、小於 4 毫米 9.5%、小於 3 毫米 3.8%。圖上標明這不能讀成「所有人都會漏一成」，能讀出來的是閾值的漏掉率會隨族群變動。第三段是分層力的比較，用同一個前瞻世代（Mayo，n=1,163，45 歲以上，2013 到 2019）畫成六條長條：年齡 60 歲以上 17.7%（95% CI 13.0 到 22.3）、反覆出血 14.7%（11.0 到 18.3）、停經後出血整體的內膜癌 7.9%（593 人中 47 例，另有內膜上皮內贅瘤 18 例，3.0%）、內膜厚度大於 4 毫米 5.8%（1.3 到 10.3）、內膜厚度小於等於 4 毫米 3.6%（0.9 到 8.6）、停經前異常出血的內膜癌 1.2%（570 人中 7 例，另有內膜上皮內贅瘤 8 例，1.4%）。圖上註明灰色那兩條是同一個世代裡「初次停經後出血、依演算法應先做超音波」的次族群，終點是癌或內膜上皮內贅瘤，兩條幾乎一樣高，也就是在這群人身上內膜厚度沒有給出有意義的分層，年齡那兩條才拉得開；並註明各列的次族群與終點定義不完全相同，數點不可互減。第四段是什麼情況要取到組織：停經後出血本身就是決定今天怎麼取到組織的時刻；切片良性但出血還在或又出現了，指引寫的是要進一步做子宮鏡加擴刮；門診取樣以擴刮或子宮切除為對照時偵測內膜癌 99.6%（停經前 91%），所有裝置特異度超過 98%（39 篇、7,914 人）；把對照換成子宮鏡加病理，敏感度掉到 90%（50 到 100），非典型增生 82%（56 到 94），把良性息肉也算進去只剩 39%（21 到 69），分母是 12 篇、1,029 人；同一份分析裡取樣失敗 11%（1 到 53%）、檢體不足 31%（7 到 76%），這些人當中有 7%（0 到 18%）最後找到內膜癌或癌前病變。圖的最後是一段說明：「不能等」靠的不是「拖久會變晚期」。這張圖沒有畫任何一條時間到期別的箭頭，因為 FIGO 2025 年的子宮體癌報告自己寫，等待手術分期的時間對存活的影響是 controversial，而且只看低惡性度的內膜癌時，等待時間與較差的存活沒有關聯。這張圖要說的只有三件事：這個族群裡本來就有大約十分之一是癌、內膜癌的病人裡九成以這個症狀表現、查清楚它只需要一次門診檢查。
en_alt: Schematic on postmenopausal bleeding: the two directions of the probability, where ultrasound sits, and what gets tissue taken. The first section gives both directions from one meta-analysis (Clarke 2018: 129 studies, 34,432 women with postmenopausal bleeding, 6,358 women with endometrial cancer, 40,790 in total). From the cancer back to the symptom, 91 per cent of women with endometrial cancer present with postmenopausal bleeding, 95 per cent confidence interval 87 to 93 per cent, all stages. From the symptom forward to the cancer, 9 per cent of women with postmenopausal bleeding are diagnosed with endometrial cancer, 95 per cent confidence interval 8 to 11 per cent. That 9 per cent moves with the population: by hormone therapy use it runs from 7 per cent (6 to 9) to 12 per cent (9 to 15), heterogeneity p less than 0.001; by region it is 5 per cent in North America (3 to 11) and 13 per cent in Western Europe (9 to 19), p equal to 0.09. The figure notes that this is the denominator of women who have already bled and already come to be seen, not a whole-population risk. The second section places ultrasound, and states on the figure that there is no arrow reading "thickness normal, go home and watch": ultrasound has one job here, helping decide whether to take tissue today and whether to go straight to hysteroscopy. Three panels must be read together. The first is what the threshold can do: at 5 mm, sensitivity 96.2 per cent (92.3 to 98.1) and specificity only 51.5 per cent (42.3 to 60.7), from 44 studies, 17,339 women with postmenopausal bleeding and 1,341 cancers (7.7 per cent); specificity is pulled down by hormone use, 92 per cent (90 to 94) in women not on hormone therapy and 77 per cent (75 to 79) in women on it, from 35 studies and 5,892 women; recomputed from individual patient data, overall discrimination is only AUC 0.82 to 0.84, the authors wrote that previous meta-analyses had probably overestimated its diagnostic accuracy, and they advised a 3 mm cut-off for exclusion. The second panel is the guideline text: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 734 of 2018 states that an endometrial thickness of 4 mm or less has a greater than 99 per cent negative predictive value for endometrial cancer; the same document also states that transvaginal ultrasonography is not an appropriate screening tool for postmenopausal women without bleeding, and that a thickness above 4 mm found incidentally without bleeding need not routinely trigger evaluation. The third panel is where the threshold misses, drawn as four bars of false-negative probability from Doll 2024 (1,494 women, 210 endometrial cancers, a single population of Black women): thickness under 5 mm gives 12.4 per cent in the postmenopausal bleeding subgroup (95 per cent CI 7.8 to 18.5) and 11.4 per cent in the whole cohort (24 of 210 cancers missed), under 4 mm 9.5 per cent and under 3 mm 3.8 per cent. The figure states that this cannot be read as everyone losing one in ten, and that what it shows is that the miss rate of a threshold varies by population. The third section compares stratifying power within one prospective cohort (Mayo, n=1,163, aged 45 and over, 2013 to 2019), as six bars: aged 60 and over 17.7 per cent (95 per cent CI 13.0 to 22.3), recurrent bleeding 14.7 per cent (11.0 to 18.3), postmenopausal bleeding overall with cancer 7.9 per cent (47 of 593, with a further 18 cases, 3.0 per cent, of endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia), endometrial thickness above 4 mm 5.8 per cent (1.3 to 10.3), endometrial thickness 4 mm or less 3.6 per cent (0.9 to 8.6), and premenopausal abnormal bleeding with cancer 1.2 per cent (7 of 570, with a further 8 cases, 1.4 per cent, of endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia). The figure notes that the two grey bars come from the subgroup with a first episode of postmenopausal bleeding in whom the algorithm called for ultrasound first, with cancer or endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia as the endpoint; that they are almost the same height, so thickness gave no useful stratification in these women while the two age-related bars do separate; and that the subgroups and endpoint definitions differ, so the values must not be subtracted from one another. The fourth section is what gets tissue taken: postmenopausal bleeding is itself the moment for deciding how tissue is obtained today; a benign biopsy with persistent or recurrent bleeding calls for hysteroscopy with dilation and curettage in the guideline text; office sampling detects endometrial cancer in 99.6 per cent against curettage or hysterectomy as the reference (91 per cent before the menopause) with specificity above 98 per cent for every device (39 studies, 7,914 women); changing the reference to hysteroscopy with histology drops sensitivity to 90 per cent (50 to 100), atypical hyperplasia to 82 per cent (56 to 94) and endometrial disease including benign polyps to 39 per cent (21 to 69), from 12 studies and 1,029 women; and in that same analysis sampling failed in 11 per cent (1 to 53) and was insufficient in 31 per cent (7 to 76), of whom 7 per cent (0 to 18) were eventually found to have endometrial cancer or a pre-cancer. The figure closes with a statement that the case for not waiting does not rest on the claim that waiting makes the stage worse. No arrow runs from time to stage, because the FIGO 2025 report on cancer of the corpus uteri says in its own words that the effect of waiting time for surgical staging on survival is controversial, and that when only low-grade endometrial cancer is considered, waiting time was not associated with worse survival. The figure argues three things and no more: roughly one in ten of this group has cancer, nine in ten women with endometrial cancer present with this symptom, and settling the question takes one clinic visit.

zh_alt: 示意圖：子宮內膜癌的四個分子型——怎麼分、各佔多少、各自往哪個方向走。本圖不含任何治療含義。第一段是臨床上怎麼分：FIGO 2023 分期文件轉述 2020 年世界衛生組織第 5 版分類的做法，用三個免疫組化染色（p53、MSH6、PMS2）加上一個 POLE 致病性突變分析，分出四群：POLE 突變型、錯配修復缺損型、p53 異常型、無特定分子輪廓型。p53 的判讀定義是腫瘤細胞強核表現超過 80%、完全沒有表現但內對照保留，或罕見的明確細胞質表現。同時符合兩型時有規則：同時是 POLE 突變或錯配修復缺損、又帶次要的 p53 異常，歸為 POLE 突變型或錯配修復缺損型；分型可以在切片檢體上做，做過了不必在子宮切除檢體上重做。第二段是四型各佔多少，畫成三條比例條，並在圖上標明前兩條是後來的臨床世代，不是 TCGA。Thompson 2022（n=1,357，加拿大 10 家癌症中心與 19 家社區醫院，2016 年全部新診斷、回溯判型）：POLE 突變型 6.3%（85 例）、錯配修復缺損型 28.0%（380 例）、無特定分子輪廓型 47.4%（643 例）、p53 異常型 18.3%（249 例）。Jamieson 2023（n=2,472，單一機構與人口基礎世代合併）：7.4%（184 例）、25.8%（638 例）、49.5%（1,223 例）、17.3%（427 例）。第三條是 León-Castillo 2020（n=410，PORTEC-3 的高風險收案族群，圖上標明不可以當成一般比例使用）：12%（51 例）、33%（137 例）、32%（129 例）、23%（93 例）。同一段另有一格講 TCGA 2013 原始論文：373 例內膜癌做整合分析，其中 248 例做了外顯子定序，四群的原始名稱是 POLE ultramutated、microsatellite instability hypermutated、copy-number low、copy-number high；全文可以看到的比例只有一個，ultramutated 是 17 例、佔那 248 例的 7%，其他三型的比例在可取得的全文裡看不到，所以上面兩條臨床世代的比例不可以說成「TCGA 的比例」；四群的突變密度每百萬鹼基分別是 232、18、2.9、2.3 個突變。第三段是各自往哪個方向走，畫成四條 5 年無復發存活的長條，並在上方用大字標明「高風險族群」：PORTEC-3 高風險族群 n=410，p 小於 0.001，POLE 突變型 98%（n=51）、錯配修復缺損型 72%（n=137）、無特定分子輪廓型 74%（n=129）、p53 異常型 48%（n=93）；圖上並註明這組數字不能代表一般的內膜癌病人。同段附註另一個高風險世代 TransPORTEC（n=116）方向一致：POLE 突變 14 例與微衛星不穩定 19 例沒有任何一例遠端轉移，5 年無復發存活 93% 與 95%；p53 突變 36 例遠端轉移 50%、無復發存活 42%；無特定分子輪廓型遠端轉移 39%、無復發存活 52%，p 小於 0.001。第四段講同一個組織型底下什麼分子型都有，四個數字全部出自 Thompson 2022：漿液性癌裡是 p53 異常型的比例 91.4%；p53 異常型裡是漿液性癌的比例只有 51.8%（129／249）；低惡性度類內膜癌 954 例裡無特定分子輪廓型佔 61.7%；低惡性度類內膜癌裡是 p53 異常型的比例 2.0%（19／954）。同段並列 Huvila 2025（n=2,478 加上 7 篇系統性回顧）：在 POLE 突變型與 p53 異常型裡，分化度與組織型已經沒有預後意義；錯配修復缺損型在第 I 期內也沒有；只有在無特定分子輪廓型裡，分化度與組織型仍然有顯著的預後意義，p 小於 0.001。第五段是檢驗本身還沒普及（Thompson 2022，加拿大 2016 年全世代）：當年做了 MMR 免疫組化的比例 42%（570／1,357，各中心 3.5% 到 95.4%）、做了 p53 免疫組化的比例 21.1%（286／1,357，各中心 10.1% 到 41.9%）；回頭看，54.7% 的 MMRd 病例當年沒做 MMR 檢驗、48.2% 的 p53abn 病例當年沒做 p53 檢驗。圖的最後寫明：這張圖不含任何治療含義，它只回答怎麼分、各佔多少、往哪個方向；分子分型會不會改掉輔助治療整篇寫在另一篇；並附上 TCGA 發表十年後一篇檢討的保留說法——十年下來它對這些病人臨床處置的實質貢獻很有限，其他三群的知識並沒有明顯改變處置。
en_alt: Schematic on the four molecular groups of endometrial cancer: how they are told apart, what share each one is, and which way each points. The figure carries no treatment implication. The first section covers how the groups are assigned in practice. The FIGO 2023 staging paper restates the approach of the 2020 WHO 5th edition classification: three immunohistochemical stains (p53, MSH6, PMS2) plus one POLE pathogenic mutation analysis give four groups — POLE-mutant, mismatch repair deficient, p53-abnormal, and no specific molecular profile. p53 is read as abnormal on strong nuclear expression in more than 80 per cent of tumour cells, complete absence of expression with retained internal control, or rarely unequivocal cytoplasmic expression. There is a rule for tumours meeting more than one definition: POLE-mutant or mismatch repair deficient with a secondary p53 abnormality counts as POLE-mutant or mismatch repair deficient. The groups can be assigned on the biopsy and need not be repeated on the hysterectomy specimen. The second section gives the proportions as three stacked bars, and states on the figure that the first two are later clinical cohorts and not TCGA. Thompson 2022 (n=1,357, 10 cancer centres and 19 community hospitals in Canada, every new diagnosis in 2016, typed retrospectively): POLE-mutant 6.3 per cent (85), mismatch repair deficient 28.0 per cent (380), no specific molecular profile 47.4 per cent (643), p53-abnormal 18.3 per cent (249). Jamieson 2023 (n=2,472, a single-institution and a population-based cohort combined): 7.4 per cent (184), 25.8 per cent (638), 49.5 per cent (1,223), 17.3 per cent (427). The third bar is Leon-Castillo 2020 (n=410, the high-risk cohort recruited to PORTEC-3, labelled on the figure as not usable as a general proportion): 12 per cent (51), 33 per cent (137), 32 per cent (129), 23 per cent (93). A panel in the same section covers the original TCGA 2013 paper: 373 endometrial carcinomas analysed together, 248 of them with exome sequencing, the original group names being POLE ultramutated, microsatellite instability hypermutated, copy-number low and copy-number high; only one proportion is visible in the accessible full text, the ultramutated group at 17 tumours or 7 per cent of those 248, with the shares of the other three groups not visible there, which is why the two clinical cohorts above must not be described as the TCGA proportions; and mutation rates across the four groups of 232, 18, 2.9 and 2.3 mutations per megabase. The third section gives the direction of outcome as four bars of 5-year recurrence-free survival, under a large label reading HIGH-RISK COHORT: PORTEC-3 high-risk cohort, n=410, p less than 0.001, POLE-mutant 98 per cent (n=51), mismatch repair deficient 72 per cent (n=137), no specific molecular profile 74 per cent (n=129), p53-abnormal 48 per cent (n=93); the figure states that these numbers cannot stand for endometrial cancer in general. A note adds that a second high-risk cohort, TransPORTEC (n=116), points the same way: neither the 14 POLE-mutant nor the 19 microsatellite-unstable tumours had a single distant metastasis, with 5-year recurrence-free survival of 93 and 95 per cent; the 36 p53-mutant tumours had 50 per cent distant metastasis and 42 per cent recurrence-free survival; and the group with no specific molecular profile had 39 and 52 per cent, p less than 0.001. The fourth section shows that every molecular group turns up under one histological type, with four numbers all from Thompson 2022: 91.4 per cent of serous carcinomas are p53-abnormal; only 51.8 per cent of p53-abnormal tumours are serous (129 of 249); 61.7 per cent of the 954 low-grade endometrioid carcinomas have no specific molecular profile; and 2.0 per cent of low-grade endometrioid carcinomas are p53-abnormal (19 of 954). Alongside it, Huvila 2025 (n=2,478 plus a systematic review of 7 studies): in the POLE-mutant and p53-abnormal groups grade and histological type no longer carry prognostic meaning, nor do they in mismatch repair deficient stage I disease, and only in the group with no specific molecular profile do they still carry significant prognostic meaning, p less than 0.001. The fifth section shows that the tests themselves are not yet universal (Thompson 2022, the whole 2016 Canadian cohort): 42 per cent of cases had mismatch repair immunohistochemistry at the time (570 of 1,357, ranging from 3.5 to 95.4 per cent across centres) and 21.1 per cent had p53 immunohistochemistry (286 of 1,357, 10.1 to 41.9 per cent across centres); looking back, 54.7 per cent of mismatch repair deficient cases had had no mismatch repair test and 48.2 per cent of p53-abnormal cases had had no p53 test. The figure closes by stating that it carries no treatment implication and answers only how the groups are told apart, how common each is and which way each points, with the question of adjuvant treatment left to its own article; and it adds the measured verdict of a review published ten years after TCGA, that over that decade the practical contribution to clinical management was limited and knowledge about the other three groups had not changed management significantly.

en_alt: Schematic comparing FIGO 2009 with FIGO 2023 by drawing only the differences. It is not a complete staging table. The first section gives the scale: nine substages become twenty-one, a count from the 2025 report by FIGO itself, which also lists this as a disadvantage, saying the new system is markedly more complicated than the previous version, which may hinder adoption and make comparisons between old and new cohorts difficult. The second section sets out the three variables written into the stage. First, histological type: the 2023 system sorts types into non-aggressive (grade 1 and grade 2 endometrioid carcinoma) and aggressive (grade 3 endometrioid, serous, clear cell, undifferentiated, mixed, mesonephric-like and gastrointestinal-type mucinous carcinoma, and carcinosarcoma), so that with the same depth of myometrial invasion the two classes land in different boxes. Second, substantial lymphovascular space invasion: a non-aggressive histological type with substantial LVSI is stage IIB regardless of local tumour spread, and FIGO 2023 defines substantial as five or more vessels involved. Third, molecular classification: where the subtype is known a lower-case m and a subscript are added, with the source wording being encouraged, and if available and feasible — encouraged, not required. The third section lists the boxes the 2023 system adds or changes. Stage I is cut open: IA1 is a non-aggressive histological type confined to a polyp or to the endometrium; IA2 is a non-aggressive type with myometrial invasion under 50 per cent and no LVSI or focal LVSI only; IA3 is low-grade endometrioid carcinoma involving uterus and ovary at once and meeting four conditions — invasion no deeper than superficial, no substantial LVSI, no other metastasis, and a unilateral ovarian tumour confined to the ovary with no capsular invasion or rupture; IB is a non-aggressive type with invasion of 50 per cent or more and no LVSI or focal LVSI only; and IC is an aggressive histological type with no myometrial invasion at all. Stage II gets markedly bigger: IIA is a non-aggressive type invading the cervical stroma; IIB is a non-aggressive type with substantial LVSI regardless of local tumour spread; and IIC is an aggressive type with any myometrial invasion — the consequence being written into the source itself, that the number of women with stage II tumours will markedly increase. Two molecular annotations follow: IAm_POLEmut for POLE-mutant carcinoma confined to the uterine corpus or with cervical extension, regardless of degree of LVSI or histological type, which moves the stage down; and IICm_p53abn for p53-abnormal carcinoma confined to the uterine corpus with any myometrial invasion, with or without cervical invasion, regardless of degree of LVSI or histological type, which moves the stage up. Stage III and IV are subdivided: IIIA separates adnexal involvement from invasion of the uterine serosa; IIIB separates vaginal or parametrial involvement from pelvic peritoneal metastasis; and IIIC is subdivided by the size of nodal metastasis following TNM8, with macrometastasis above 2 mm, micrometastasis 0.2 to 2 mm and/or more than 200 cells, and isolated tumour cells recorded as pN0(i+), of which the source says the prognostic significance is unclear. The same section marks one thing that did not change: peritoneal cytology stays out of the stage. FIGO 2023 groups positive washing cytology with intraluminal tubal floating tumour fragments as a controversial issue, and the figure also carries the other half — in a cohort of 720 women, positive peritoneal cytology was associated with worse outcomes on multivariable analysis, and the authors wrote that omitting peritoneal cytology from prognostic assessment may risk undertreatment. Not entering the stage is not the same as carrying no information. The fourth section shows that the word substantial does not mean the same number in every document: FIGO 2023 uses five or more vessels, NCCN four or more, the 2022 ICCR three or more and the 2019 ISGyP three or more. On reading agreement, the intraclass correlation coefficient for whether LVSI is present at all is 0.6 and for whether it is substantial 0.56, both quoted second-hand by that review; and the FIGO 2025 report lists this among the disadvantages of the new system, saying it incorporates variables whose definitions are still evolving and which are subject to considerable interobserver variability, naming LVSI as the example. The fifth section draws how much the stage moves as eight bars: Veiga 2026 (18 centres in Spain, n=4,566) 19.9 per cent; Seo 2025 (single institution, Korea, n=2,969) 20.2 per cent; Sia 2026 (MSKCC, n=2,067) 26.0 per cent upstaged with a further 4.8 per cent downstaged; Zhao 2025 (China, n=720) 27.4 per cent; Schwameis 2023 (three centres in Austria and Italy, n=519) 27.6 per cent; Ozcelik 2026 (two centres in Turkey, n=291) 32.0 per cent; Manabe 2025 (four centres in Japan, n=1,207) 36.3 per cent; and Chen 2026 (Shanghai, n=331) 56.2 per cent. The figure notes that upstaging means landing in a higher-numbered box once a different description is applied, not that the tumour has grown, and that the cohorts cannot stand in for one another. The sixth section puts both sides together. In favour: rerun across 129,146 patients in the US National Cancer Database, 5-year overall survival for 2009 stage IIIA was 63.9 per cent, and splitting it under the 2023 system gives 88.0 per cent for IA3, 62.4 per cent for IIIA1 and 55.7 per cent for IIIA2; in a cohort of 2,067, those reassigned to the new IA3 had 5-year overall survival of 100 per cent while under the 2009 system they were stage IIIA at 70.3 per cent; and in the other direction, those labelled IICm_p53abn had 73 per cent while under the 2009 system most were merely stage II, at 86.8 per cent. Against: in a Korean cohort of 472, the 84 women with aggressive histological types were separated by neither overall nor recurrence-free survival under the 2023 system, while the 2009 system still stratified recurrence-free survival (p=0.017); in a Turkish study of 291, once the pathological factors making up the stage were adjusted for, stage migration itself no longer independently predicted survival; the MSKCC authors wrote that small numbers in each substage and concerns about over-fitting limit their analysis; and a commentary by ten gynaecological pathologists in 2024 titled "FIGO 2023 endometrial cancer staging: too much, too soon?" argues the system should first be appraised at a multi-institutional and global level with input from all relevant societies, to which FIGO replied that it has generated some controversy. The seventh section covers who adopted it and who kept the old one: the 2025 update of the ESGO, ESTRO and ESP guidelines explicitly incorporates FIGO 2023; the British Gynaecological Cancer Society and the British Association of Gynecological Pathologists have recommended continuing to use the 2009 system; and which version Taiwan uses could not be found in any official or society statement, so the figure does not say, and readers are pointed to the version printed on their own pathology report. It also carries a study from one Taiwanese medical centre: assigning a FIGO 2023 stage by conventional table look-up was correct only 58.1 per cent of the time, 62.6 per cent for obstetrician-gynaecologists using the same method, 49.0 per cent in molecular-classification scenarios and 58.3 per cent in IA3 scenarios — so nobody should convert their own report. The figure closes with two panels. The first: the randomised evidence for adjuvant treatment was recruited under the older staging systems. PORTEC-1 recruited from 1990 to 1997 with entry criteria written in the language of FIGO 1988; GOG-99 recruited FIGO stages IB, IC and II occult, and those two substages exist only in the 1988 version; PORTEC-3 recruited from 2006 to 2013 and its protocol reads FIGO 2009 stage I; whether any adjuvant trial has recruited under the 2023 version could not be established, only that the main trials found were not; and FIGO 2023 is guarded in its own words, saying that strategies to de-escalate or intensify post-operative treatment by molecular profile are being defined. The second: a change in the stage number does not by itself trigger a change in treatment, and that decision goes back to the gynaecological oncology and radiation oncology clinic; but that is not the same as saying the new system is pointless, because it addresses the genuine problem that outlooks inside one stage I differ enormously. Drop either sentence and the figure gets read the wrong way.

原文寫對中高風險與高風險的病人應該做淋巴結分期，前哨淋巴結切片是系統性廓清在分期用途上的適當替代方案。系統性淋巴結廓清：把骨盆腔、有時再加主動脈旁的淋巴結成群取下，不管看起來有沒有問題；義大利那個隨機試驗裡取出淋巴結的中位數是 30 顆（四分位距 22 到 42）對 0 顆；FIGO 2025 年報告寫，自從前哨淋巴結切片發展起來之後，做完整分期性淋巴結廓清的適應症已經很少。第二段是前哨這條路的可靠度，三個前瞻研究各有自己的分母，而且三個都以做完整廓清當對照。FIRES（Rossi 2017，美國 10 家中心含社區醫院、18 位外科醫師，臨床第 1 期、所有組織型與分化度，子宮頸注射 ICG 加機器手臂，385 人收案、340 人做完對照）：至少定位到一顆前哨淋巴結 86%（293／340）；敏感度 97.2%（95% CI 85.0 到 100），41 例淋巴結陽性中 36 例成功定位、其中 35 例的轉移在前哨被找到；陰性預測值 99.6%（97.9 到 100）；作者原文寫前哨淋巴結切片不會在 3% 的淋巴結陽性病人身上找到轉移。SENTOR（Cusimano 2021，加拿大 3 家中心，臨床第 1 期第 2 級類內膜癌或高惡性度內膜癌，156 人中 126 人高惡性度，ICG）：每位病人的定位率 97.4%（93.6 到 99.3），每半骨盆 87.5%，雙側 77.6%（70.2 到 83.8）；敏感度 96%（81 到 100），27 例淋巴結陽性中 26 例被找到；偽陰性率 4%（0 到 19），陰性預測值 99%（96 到 100）；27 例淋巴結陽性中有 7 例、也就是 26%，轉移落在傳統骨盆腔廓清範圍之外或需要免疫組化才找得到。SENTI-ENDO（Ballester 2011，法國 9 家中心前瞻世代，FIGO 第 I 到 II 期，子宮頸雙示蹤鎝加 patent blue，133 人收案、125 人可評估）：至少定位到一顆前哨淋巴結 111／125；以半骨盆為單位敏感度 100%（63 到 100）、陰性預測值 100%（95 到 100）；以病人為單位敏感度只有 84%（62 到 95）、陰性預測值 97%（91 到 99）；3 例偽陰性全部是第 2 型非類內膜的內膜癌。同一段另有一格把「漏掉」講清楚：分母是淋巴結陽性的病人。FIRES 作者的原文是，前哨淋巴結切片不會在 3% 的淋巴結陽性病人身上找到轉移；SENTOR 的偽陰性率是 4%，也就是 27 例中的 1 例。所以「前哨和全部拿掉一樣準」不是這張圖的意思，正確的說法是在前瞻研究裡漏掉的比例是 3% 到 4%，而且非類內膜癌的偽陰性風險比較高。第三段是示蹤劑的隨機對照：FILM 隨機試驗在同一位病人身上同時打兩種染劑，子宮頸癌與子宮體癌臨床第 1 期，180 人隨機、176 人可評估；依方案分析的 163 人、485 顆淋巴結，綠色的吲哚菁綠找到 471 顆（97%），藍色染劑找到 226 顆（47%），差 50 個百分點（95% CI 39 到 62），p 小於 0.0001；兩者找到的東西經病理確認確實是淋巴組織的比例沒有差別，p 等於 0.33。第四段把全面廓清的兩個隨機試驗放上天平。得到什麼：找到淋巴結轉移的比例 13.3% 對 3.2%，差 10.1 個百分點（95% CI 5.3 到 14.9），p 小於 0.001；取出淋巴結中位數 30 顆對 0 顆。付出什麼：發生早期或晚期術後併發症的人數 81 人對 34 人，p 等於 0.001，同一個 514 人的試驗。沒有換到的是存活：ASTEC（n=1,408，4 國 85 中心）總存活風險比 1.16（95% CI 0.87 到 1.54，p 等於 0.31），5 年絕對差 1 個百分點（−4 到 6）；無復發存活風險比 1.35（1.06 到 1.73，p 等於 0.017），方向反而偏向不做廓清，校正基線與病理後總存活 1.04（0.74 到 1.45）、無復發存活 1.25（0.93 到 1.66），兩者都不顯著；Benedetti Panici（n=514）5 年無病存活 81.0% 對 81.7%，首次事件風險比 1.10（0.70 到 1.71，p 等於 0.68）；5 年總存活 85.9% 對 90.0%，死亡風險比 1.20（0.70 到 2.07，p 等於 0.50）。ASTEC 的結論原文是：骨盆腔淋巴結廓清不能作為臨床試驗以外的常規治療性手術而被推薦。同段並附一格說明：ASTEC 的術後放療是獨立隨機分派的，與淋巴結結果無關，所以它回答的是廓清這個動作本身有沒有治療效果，不是知道淋巴結狀態有沒有用；兩個試驗都是前哨淋巴結時代之前收的，Benedetti Panici 只做骨盆腔、沒有做主動脈旁，術後治療也不是隨機化的。第五段是「換到什麼」，這一格刻意不放數字：下肢的水腫在改做前哨之後確實少一些，少多少取決於誰在量、怎麼量，同一批人用四種量法會得到完全不同的結論，所以這張圖不放任何一個水腫的百分比，並用一個箭頭指向〈下肢淋巴水腫，怎麼防怎麼處理〉那一篇。第六段把上一段的微創對照放在同一張圖上：LACE（n=760，第 I 期類內膜癌）4.5 年無病存活 81.6% 對 81.3%，差 0.3 個百分點（95% CI −5.5 到 6.1），達到預設的等價；LAP2（n=2,616）3 年復發率 11.4% 對 10.2%、5 年整體存活兩組都是 89.8%，但沒有達到自己預設的非劣性門檻，風險比 1.14、90% 下界 0.92、95% 上界 1.46；對照組是子宮頸癌的 LACC，微創 4.5 年無病存活 86.0% 對開腹 96.5%——圖上標明 LACC 是不同的癌別、不同的手術（根除性子宮切除），不可以拿來互比。圖的最後列出這張圖不能讀成的三句話：第一，前哨和全部拿掉一樣準——不是，前瞻研究裡漏掉的是 3% 到 4%，非類內膜癌的偽陰性風險更高；第二，淋巴結不用管——不是，兩個隨機試驗證明的是廓清這個動作沒有治療效果，不是淋巴結狀態不重要；第三，所以我應該要求做或不做哪一種——這張圖給的是問題清單，怎麼做由婦癌科依組織型、分化度與影像決定。
en_alt: Schematic comparing sentinel lymph node biopsy with systematic lymphadenectomy: what each route does, what is traded for what, and what the sentinel route misses. The figure carries no leg lymphoedema figure of any kind. The first section draws the two routes. Sentinel lymph node biopsy: a tracer is injected into the cervix to find the few nodes the tumour would reach first, only those nodes are removed and pathology examines them in more detail, with immunohistochemistry where needed; FIGO 2023 states that lymph node staging should be performed in intermediate-high and high-risk patients and that sentinel lymph node biopsy is an adequate alternative to systematic lymphadenectomy for staging purposes. Systematic lymphadenectomy: the pelvic nodes, sometimes with the para-aortic nodes, are removed as a group whether or not they look abnormal; in the Italian randomised trial the median number removed was 30 (interquartile range 22 to 42) against 0; and the FIGO 2025 report states that since the development of sentinel lymph node biopsy the indications for full surgical staging lymphadenectomy are scarce. The second section gives the reliability of the sentinel route from three prospective studies, each with its own denominator, all three using full lymphadenectomy as the reference. FIRES (Rossi 2017; 10 US centres including community hospitals, 18 surgeons, clinical stage 1, all histological types and grades, cervical ICG injection with robotic assistance, 385 enrolled and 340 completing the reference standard): at least one sentinel node mapped in 86 per cent (293 of 340); sensitivity 97.2 per cent (95 per cent CI 85.0 to 100), with 36 of 41 node-positive patients mapping successfully and the metastasis found in the sentinel node in 35 of those; negative predictive value 99.6 per cent (97.9 to 100); and the words of the authors themselves, that sentinel lymph node biopsy will not identify metastases in 3 per cent of patients with node-positive disease. SENTOR (Cusimano 2021; 3 Canadian centres, clinical stage 1 grade 2 endometrioid or high-grade endometrial cancer, 126 of 156 high-grade, ICG): detection rate per patient 97.4 per cent (93.6 to 99.3), 87.5 per cent per hemipelvis, bilateral 77.6 per cent (70.2 to 83.8); sensitivity 96 per cent (81 to 100), with 26 of 27 node-positive patients identified; false-negative rate 4 per cent (0 to 19) and negative predictive value 99 per cent (96 to 100); and in 7 of those 27 node-positive patients, 26 per cent, the metastasis lay outside the conventional pelvic dissection field or needed immunohistochemistry to be found. SENTI-ENDO (Ballester 2011; a prospective cohort across 9 French centres, FIGO stage I to II, dual cervical tracer of technetium plus patent blue with systematic pelvic lymphadenectomy, 133 enrolled and 125 evaluable): at least one sentinel node mapped in 111 of 125; sensitivity per hemipelvis 100 per cent (63 to 100) with negative predictive value 100 per cent (95 to 100); sensitivity per patient only 84 per cent (62 to 95) with negative predictive value 97 per cent (91 to 99); and all three false negatives were type 2, non-endometrioid, endometrial cancer. A panel in the same section states the miss rate precisely, with node-positive patients as the denominator: FIRES puts it at 3 per cent, in the words of the authors that sentinel lymph node biopsy will not identify metastases in 3 per cent of patients with node-positive disease, and the SENTOR false-negative rate is 4 per cent, 1 of 27. So the figure does not say that sentinel biopsy is as accurate as taking them all; the accurate sentence is that the miss rate in prospective studies is 3 to 4 per cent and that the false-negative risk is higher in non-endometrioid cancer. The third section gives the randomised comparison of tracers: the FILM trial injected both dyes into the same patient (clinical stage 1 cervical and uterine cancer, 180 randomised, 176 evaluable); in the per-protocol analysis of 163 patients and 485 nodes, indocyanine green found 471 nodes (97 per cent) and blue dye found 226 (47 per cent), a difference of 50 percentage points (95 per cent CI 39 to 62), p less than 0.0001, while the share of what was found that pathology confirmed as lymphatic tissue did not differ, p equal to 0.33. The fourth section puts the two randomised trials of full lymphadenectomy on one balance. What it gains: nodal metastasis was found in 13.3 per cent against 3.2 per cent, a difference of 10.1 percentage points (95 per cent CI 5.3 to 14.9), p less than 0.001; and the median number of nodes removed was 30 against 0. What it costs: 81 women against 34 had an early or late post-operative complication, p equal to 0.001, in the same trial of 514. What it does not buy is survival: in ASTEC (n=1,408, 85 centres in 4 countries) overall survival gave a hazard ratio of 1.16 (95 per cent CI 0.87 to 1.54, p equal to 0.31) with an absolute difference at 5 years of 1 percentage point (−4 to 6), and recurrence-free survival a hazard ratio of 1.35 (1.06 to 1.73, p equal to 0.017) pointing if anything towards not dissecting, with both becoming non-significant after adjustment for baseline and pathology at 1.04 (0.74 to 1.45) and 1.25 (0.93 to 1.66); and in Benedetti Panici (n=514) 5-year disease-free survival was 81.0 per cent against 81.7 per cent with a hazard ratio for a first event of 1.10 (0.70 to 1.71), p equal to 0.68, and 5-year overall survival 85.9 per cent against 90.0 per cent with a hazard ratio for death of 1.20 (0.70 to 2.07), p equal to 0.50. The ASTEC conclusion is quoted: pelvic lymphadenectomy cannot be recommended as a routine procedure for therapeutic purposes outside of clinical trials. A further panel states what these trials do not answer: radiotherapy in ASTEC was randomised independently of the nodal result, so the trial answers whether the dissection itself has a therapeutic effect rather than whether knowing the nodal status is useful; both trials recruited before the sentinel era; Benedetti Panici dissected the pelvis only with no para-aortic dissection and did not randomise post-operative treatment. The fifth section is what is traded, and it deliberately carries no numbers: swelling in the leg is genuinely less common after sentinel biopsy, and how much less depends on who measures and how, because the same group of women measured four different ways gives entirely different conclusions; an arrow points instead to the article on leg lymphoedema, how to prevent it and how to manage it. The sixth section keeps the minimally invasive comparison from the previous part of the article in the same frame: LACE (n=760, stage I endometrioid) gave 4.5-year disease-free survival of 81.6 per cent against 81.3 per cent, a difference of 0.3 percentage points (95 per cent CI −5.5 to 6.1), meeting its pre-specified equivalence margin; LAP2 (n=2,616) gave a 3-year recurrence rate of 11.4 per cent against 10.2 per cent and 5-year overall survival of 89.8 per cent in both arms, yet did not meet its own pre-specified non-inferiority threshold, hazard ratio 1.14 with a 90 per cent lower bound of 0.92 and a 95 per cent upper bound of 1.46; and the contrast is LACC in cervical cancer, where 4.5-year disease-free survival was 86.0 per cent with minimally invasive surgery against 96.5 per cent with open surgery — with the figure stating that LACC is a different cancer and a different operation, radical hysterectomy, and that the two must not be compared directly. The figure closes with three sentences it must not be read as. First, that sentinel biopsy is as accurate as taking them all — it is not, the miss rate in prospective studies is 3 to 4 per cent and higher in non-endometrioid cancer. Second, that nodes do not matter — they do, and what the two randomised trials show is that the dissection has no therapeutic effect, not that nodal status is unimportant. Third, that the reader should ask for one route or the other — the figure is a list of questions, and which route is used is decided by the gynaecological oncology team from histological type, grade and imaging.

zh_alt: 示意圖：三個 PORTEC 試驗各回答一題，圖上沒有任何可以自己打勾的判準欄位。第一張大卡片是 PORTEC-1（n=715，FIGO 1988／2009 版第 1 期、類內膜、未做淋巴結廓清），問的是術後骨盆腔放療 46 Gy 換到什麼、付出什麼；三組橫條共用同一把 0 到 100% 的尺，每組上面一條是骨盆腔放療 46 Gy、下面一條是不做進一步治療。第一組是 5 年局部區域復發：放療 4%，觀察 14%，p 小於 0.001，放療組少 10 個百分點，這是放療真正買到的局部控制。第二組是 5 年整體存活：放療 81%，觀察 85%，p 等於 0.31，兩條一樣長；原文結論句是術後放療降低局部區域復發、對整體存活沒有影響。第三組是治療相關併發症：放療 25%，觀察 6%，p 小於 0.0001，放療組多 19 個百分點；三分之二是第 1 級，第 3 到 4 級併發症共 8 人、其中 7 人在放療組、佔該組 2%。卡片下方有一段字：三格要一起讀，只看第一格會讀成當然要照，只看第二格會讀成反正不延長存活，只看第三格會讀成放療很傷別碰；三格放在一起才是這個試驗的意思——放療買到的是局部控制，付出的是併發症，而它沒有把存活曲線拉開。第二張卡片是 PORTEC-2（n=427，高中度風險，FIGO 1988 版第 I 或 IIA 期），問的是可不可以把範圍縮小到只照陰道那一小段。5 年陰道復發：陰道近接治療 1.8%，骨盆腔外照射 46 Gy 分 23 次 1.6%，風險比 0.78（0.17 到 3.49），p 等於 0.74。旁邊畫了一把非劣性的尺：零點在左端，預設的非劣性邊界是 6 個百分點，觀察到的差值是加 0.2 個百分點，落在邊界之內。圖上寫著非劣性成立的意思是差值沒有超過事先講好的那條線，不是兩組一樣好；信賴區間 0.17 到 3.49 很寬，這個人數不足以證明兩者相同。同一張卡片另有一格誠實對照：5 年局部區域復發（陰道或骨盆腔）是近接治療 5.1% 對外照射 2.1%，風險比 2.08（0.71 到 6.09），p 等於 0.17，點估計不利於近接治療，只是沒有達到統計顯著；10 年的骨盆腔復發另有一張圖。第三張卡片是 PORTEC-3（n=660，高風險，FIGO 2009 版），問的是高風險的人在放療上面加化療換到什麼。10 年整體存活：化放療 74.4%，單純放療 67.3%。下面畫一條對數尺的風險比圖，虛線標出 1，校正後風險比 0.73、95% 信賴區間 0.54 到 0.97、p 等於 0.032，信賴區間沒有跨過 1。同一張卡片的誠實對照寫著：5 年的主要分析總存活是 81.8% 對 76.7%，風險比 0.76，p 等於 0.11，沒有達到統計顯著；10 年那一頁的益處集中在第 III 期與漿液性組織型。圖的最下面是一個金框方塊：這張圖不是判準表，也不是給你自己對號入座用的。三個試驗的收案條件、分期版本、風險族群都不一樣——PORTEC-1 沒有做淋巴結廓清，PORTEC-2 收的是高中度風險，PORTEC-3 收的是高風險，三格之間不可以直接比較。風險分組有正式的名字與定義，寫在正文裡；分組要同時看期別與版本、組織型、分化度、肌層侵犯、淋巴血管腔侵犯的量、有沒有做淋巴結分期，還有分子分型。這是要別人幫你算的問題。
en_alt: Schematic: three PORTEC trials, one question each, with nothing on the figure that a reader could tick off for herself. The first, full-width card is PORTEC-1 (n=715, FIGO 1988/2009 stage 1, endometrioid, no lymph node dissection), asking what postoperative pelvic radiotherapy at 46 Gy buys and what it costs. Three pairs of horizontal bars share one 0 to 100 per cent scale; in each pair the upper bar is pelvic radiotherapy 46 Gy and the lower bar is no further treatment. First pair, 5-year locoregional recurrence: 4 per cent with radiotherapy against 14 per cent with observation, p < 0.001, ten percentage points fewer - local control is what the treatment actually buys. Second pair, 5-year overall survival: 81 against 85 per cent, p = 0.31, the two bars the same length; the published conclusion is that postoperative radiotherapy reduces locoregional recurrence but has no impact on overall survival. Third pair, treatment-related complications: 25 against 6 per cent, p < 0.0001, nineteen percentage points more in the radiotherapy arm; two-thirds were grade 1, and of 8 grade 3-4 complications in all, 7 were in the radiotherapy arm, 2 per cent of that arm. Beneath the card a line reads: the three boxes have to be read together - read only the first and you get "of course I should have it", only the second and you get "it does not prolong life", only the third and you get "radiotherapy is harmful"; together they are what the trial says, that radiotherapy buys local control, costs complications, and did not pull the survival curves apart. The second card is PORTEC-2 (n=427, high-intermediate risk, FIGO 1988 stage I or IIA), asking whether the field can be shrunk to the top of the vagina alone. 5-year vaginal recurrence: vaginal brachytherapy 1.8 per cent against pelvic external beam radiotherapy 46 Gy in 23 fractions 1.6 per cent, hazard ratio 0.78 (0.17 to 3.49), p = 0.74. Alongside is a non-inferiority scale: zero at the left, the pre-set margin of 6 percentage points marked with a dashed line, and the observed difference of plus 0.2 percentage points sitting well inside it. The figure states that non-inferiority means the difference did not cross the line agreed in advance, not that the two treatments are the same, and that a confidence interval of 0.17 to 3.49 is wide - this many patients cannot show that they are equal. The same card carries the other side of the trial: 5-year locoregional recurrence, in the vagina or the pelvis, was 5.1 per cent with brachytherapy against 2.1 per cent with external beam radiotherapy, hazard ratio 2.08 (0.71 to 6.09), p = 0.17, a point estimate that favours external beam without reaching statistical significance; the 10-year pelvic figures are in a separate diagram. The third card is PORTEC-3 (n=660, high risk, FIGO 2009), asking what adding chemotherapy to radiotherapy buys in high-risk disease. 10-year overall survival: chemoradiotherapy 74.4 per cent against radiotherapy alone 67.3 per cent. Below, a hazard ratio plotted on a log scale with a dashed line at 1 shows an adjusted hazard ratio of 0.73, 95 per cent confidence interval 0.54 to 0.97, p = 0.032, the interval not crossing 1. The other side of that trial is also given: in the 5-year primary analysis overall survival was 81.8 against 76.7 per cent, hazard ratio 0.76, p = 0.11, not statistically significant, and at 10 years the benefit is concentrated in stage III disease and serous histology. At the foot of the figure a gold-bordered panel states that this is not a checklist and not for placing yourself in a box: the three trials differ in entry criteria, staging version and risk group - PORTEC-1 had no lymph node dissection, PORTEC-2 recruited high-intermediate risk, PORTEC-3 high risk - so the boxes must not be compared with one another; the risk groups have formal names and definitions set out in the article, and assigning one means weighing stage and its version, histological type, grade, depth of myometrial invasion, the amount of lymphovascular space invasion, whether nodes were staged and the molecular profile. It is a calculation for someone else to do with you.

zh_alt: 示意圖：陰道近接治療是什麼，以及 PORTEC-2 的兩張帳單。第一部分是一張剖面示意圖，畫的是子宮已經切除之後的陰道：上方用虛線畫出已被切除的子宮並標「子宮已切除」，陰道殘端封在上端，一根單管陰道套管從下方置入、頂端頂到殘端。陰道上三分之一連同往深處 5 毫米的一圈組織被標成標靶區，標示「標靶：陰道上三分之一、深度 5 mm」，另標「處方點在距施用器表面 0.5 公分」，並註明先做陰道檢查確認殘端癒合、再依陰道大小與形狀選施用器，通常用的是陰道套管。療程的形狀畫成一排圓點：單獨使用是 21 到 24 Gy 分 3 到 4 次，第 4 次視處方而定；外照射之後的加強照射是 8 到 11 Gy 分 2 到 3 次。旁註寫著各家處方不完全一樣：美國近接治療學會 2014 年調查 289 位醫師，96.2% 使用高劑量率，最常治療的陰道長度是 4 公分（31.0%），單獨使用時最常見的兩種處方是 7 Gy 照 3 次（到 0.5 公分深）與 6 Gy 照 5 次（到陰道表面）；每一次要花多久、間隔幾天、當天能不能自己回家，查不到可以引用的正式數字。第二部分是 PORTEC-2（n=427，高中度風險，FIGO 1988 版第 I 或 IIA 期）的兩張帳單，並排呈現。左邊「換到什麼」：放療結束時的急性第 1 到 2 級腸胃道毒性，陰道近接治療 12.6%（27／215），骨盆腔外照射 53.8%（112／208），畫成兩條橫條；生活品質研究（348 人可評估）裡近接治療組的社會功能較好（p 小於 0.002），腹瀉、糞便滲漏、必須待在廁所附近、因腸道症狀限制日常活動的分數也較低（p 小於 0.001）。陰道復發：5 年 1.8% 對 1.6%，非劣性成立（預設邊界 6 個百分點），風險比 0.78（0.17 到 3.49），p 等於 0.74；10 年 3.4% 對 2.4%，p 等於 0.55；10 年整體存活 69.5% 對 67.6%，p 等於 0.72。並註明非劣性證明的是沒有差到超過事先講好的那條線，不是一樣好。右邊「沒有換到什麼」用紅框畫出：10 年骨盆腔復發，近接治療 6.3%，外照射 0.9%，p 等於 0.004，兩條橫條的方向與左邊相反；多數合併遠端轉移，只發生在骨盆腔而沒有合併遠端轉移的那一群是 2.5% 對 0.5%（p 等於 0.10）。5 年局部區域復發（陰道或骨盆腔）是 5.1% 對 2.1%，風險比 2.08（0.71 到 6.09），p 等於 0.17，這個方向在 5 年那一頁就看得到，只是當時沒有達到統計顯著。10 年那篇論文也指出誰不適合把範圍縮到最小：L1CAM 或 p53 突變型表現、以及 substantial LVSI（顯著的淋巴血管腔侵犯）的人，外照射提供比較好的骨盆腔控制。第三部分是與子宮頸癌腔內近接治療的對照，左右各一張示意圖：左邊是子宮內膜癌術後，子宮已切除，一根單管套管在陰道裡，標「單管」；右邊是子宮頸癌根治性治療，子宮還在，用 tandem（子宮內管）加上 ring 或 ovoid、必要時再加組織插種針，子宮頸周圍用虛線圈出 CTV-HR，標「多管」。下面的對照表六列：子宮還在嗎——已經切除、治療的是陰道殘端，對子宮還在、腫瘤在子宮頸；施用器——單管陰道套管，對 tandem 加 ring 或 ovoid、必要時加組織插種針；標靶——陰道上三分之一、深度 5 mm，對 CTV-HR 影像導引、每一次重畫的殘存腫瘤體積；劑量——21 到 24 Gy 分 3 到 4 次（單獨使用）、外照後加強 8 到 11 Gy 分 2 到 3 次，對 CTV-HR 的 D90 規劃目標大於 90 Gy EQD2₁₀、處方劑量下限大於 85 Gy（含外照）；搭配的外照射——多數情況不做，對 45 Gy 分 25 次幾乎必做且多合併同步化療；健保支付項目——37008B 安裝近接治療器（簡單，單管）1,650 點加 37018B 遙控後荷式近距治療（簡單）4,126 點，對 37007B 安裝近接治療器（複雜，多管）3,236 點加 37019B 遙控後荷式近距治療（複雜）6,600 點。表下註明支付標準自己就把兩者分成簡單／單管與複雜／多管兩組代碼；點數是表定值，不是病人要付的金額，實際怎麼申報、有沒有自費項目要問醫務課或個管師。
en_alt: Schematic: what vaginal brachytherapy is, and the two bills from PORTEC-2. The first part is a cross-sectional drawing of the vagina after the uterus has been removed: the removed uterus is drawn in a dashed outline and labelled "uterus removed", the vaginal cuff is closed at the top, and a single vaginal cylinder is inserted from below with its tip against the cuff. The upper third of the vagina together with a rim of tissue 5 mm deep is marked as the target, labelled "target: upper third of the vagina, to a depth of 5 mm", with a second label "prescribed at 0.5 cm from the applicator surface", and a note that a vaginal examination first confirms the cuff has healed and that the size and shape of the vagina guide the choice of applicator, a cylinder usually being used. The shape of the course is drawn as a row of dots: used alone, 21 to 24 Gy in 3 to 4 fractions, the fourth depending on the prescription; as a boost after external beam radiotherapy, 8 to 11 Gy in 2 to 3 fractions. A note records that prescriptions differ between centres: in the American Brachytherapy Society 2014 survey of 289 clinicians, 96.2 per cent used high dose rate, the most commonly treated vaginal length was 4 cm (31.0 per cent), and used alone the two commonest prescriptions were 7 Gy in 3 fractions to 0.5 cm depth and 6 Gy in 5 fractions to the vaginal surface; how long each session takes, how many days apart they are and whether you can go home the same day could not be sourced. The second part sets two bills from PORTEC-2 (n=427, high-intermediate risk, FIGO 1988 stage I or IIA) side by side. On the left, what it buys: acute grade 1-2 gastrointestinal toxicity at the end of treatment, 12.6 per cent (27 of 215) with vaginal brachytherapy against 53.8 per cent (112 of 208) with pelvic external beam radiotherapy, drawn as two bars; in the quality-of-life study (348 evaluable) the brachytherapy arm had better social functioning (p < 0.002) and lower scores for diarrhoea, faecal leakage, having to stay near a toilet and limitation of daily activities by bowel symptoms (p < 0.001). Vaginal recurrence: 1.8 against 1.6 per cent at 5 years, non-inferiority met against a pre-set margin of 6 percentage points, hazard ratio 0.78 (0.17 to 3.49), p = 0.74; 3.4 against 2.4 per cent at 10 years, p = 0.55; and 10-year overall survival 69.5 against 67.6 per cent, p = 0.72 - with a note that non-inferiority proves the difference did not cross a line agreed in advance, not that the two are the same. On the right, in a red-bordered panel, what it does not buy: 10-year pelvic recurrence 6.3 per cent with brachytherapy against 0.9 per cent with external beam radiotherapy, p = 0.004, the two bars running the opposite way to those on the left; most were accompanied by distant metastases, and pelvic recurrence without distant metastases was 2.5 against 0.5 per cent (p = 0.10). 5-year locoregional recurrence, in the vagina or the pelvis, was 5.1 against 2.1 per cent, hazard ratio 2.08 (0.71 to 6.09), p = 0.17: the direction was already visible at 5 years without reaching statistical significance then. The 10-year paper also names who should not have the field shrunk to its smallest: with L1CAM or mutant-pattern p53 expression, and with substantial lymphovascular space invasion, external beam radiotherapy gave better pelvic control. The third part contrasts this with intracavitary brachytherapy for cervical cancer, with a drawing on each side: on the left, after endometrial cancer surgery, the uterus gone and a single cylinder in the vagina, labelled "single channel"; on the right, definitive treatment of cervical cancer, the uterus still in place, a tandem with ring or ovoids and interstitial needles where needed, and a dashed outline around the cervix marking CTV-HR, labelled "multi-channel". A six-row table follows. Is the uterus still there: already removed, the vaginal cuff treated, against still there with the tumour in the cervix. Applicator: a single vaginal cylinder, against a tandem plus ring or ovoids with interstitial needles where needed. Target: upper third of the vagina to a depth of 5 mm, against CTV-HR, image-guided and redrawn at each fraction. Dose: 21 to 24 Gy in 3 to 4 fractions used alone, or 8 to 11 Gy in 2 to 3 fractions as a boost after external beam radiotherapy, against a CTV-HR D90 planning aim above 90 Gy EQD2 with alpha/beta 10 and a prescribed dose no lower than 85 Gy including external beam. External beam alongside: usually none, against 45 Gy in 25 fractions almost always, usually with concurrent chemotherapy. Taiwanese national health insurance items: 37008B applicator insertion (simple, single channel) 1,650 points plus 37018B remote afterloading brachytherapy (simple) 4,126 points, against 37007B applicator insertion (complex, multi-channel) 3,236 points plus 37019B remote afterloading brachytherapy (complex) 6,600 points. Below the table a note records that the fee schedule itself splits the two into simple/single-channel and complex/multi-channel codes, and that points are tabulated values rather than what a patient pays, so how a course is claimed and whether anything is self-paid is a question for the hospital billing office or the case manager.

en_alt: Schematic: where the molecular profile pushes adjuvant treatment, and why direction is not the same as strength. The upper block shows the four PORTEC-3 classes (10-year molecular analysis, 411 of 660 evaluable, high-risk population, FIGO 2009), the whole block labelled "all post-hoc analyses". POLE mutant (n=51): 10-year overall survival 98.0 per cent (94.3 to 100.0); chemoradiotherapy 100.0 against radiotherapy alone 96.4 per cent, compared by log-rank with p = 0.40 and no hazard ratio reported for this box; direction marked de-escalation, with the authors concluding that irrespective of stage, and on the basis of excellent recurrence-free survival, de-escalation should be recommended for POLE mutant cancers, preferably in a study setting. MMRd, mismatch repair deficient (n=139): 10-year overall survival 71.7 per cent (64.2 to 80.0); chemoradiotherapy 68.7 against radiotherapy alone 74.4 per cent, adjusted hazard ratio 1.34, 95 per cent confidence interval 0.71 to 2.55, p = 0.37, drawn as an interval crossing the dashed line at 1; this box is labelled "unfavourable direction, not significant, small n", with a note that none of the three labels may be dropped, so it can neither be read as chemotherapy helping here nor, in the other direction, as chemotherapy not being needed. NSMP, no specific molecular profile (n=122): 10-year overall survival 77.9 per cent (70.7 to 85.8); chemoradiotherapy 81.2 against radiotherapy alone 74.1 per cent, adjusted hazard ratio 0.60 (0.27 to 1.32), p = 0.21, the interval again crossing 1 and the box labelled not significant; the authors add that for oestrogen-receptor-positive tumours the benefit of chemotherapy may be smaller than hypothesised and hormonal therapy could be an alternative. p53 abnormal (n=99): 10-year overall survival 45.1 per cent (36.2 to 56.1); chemoradiotherapy 52.7 against radiotherapy alone 36.6 per cent, adjusted hazard ratio 0.52 (0.30 to 0.91), p = 0.021, the interval not crossing 1, direction marked escalation and the box carrying a "post-hoc analysis" tag; 10-year recurrence-free survival was 52.6 against 37.0 per cent, adjusted hazard ratio 0.42 (0.24 to 0.74), p = 0.0027. The middle block is PORTEC-4a, tagged "has read out" and "non-inferiority": n=564 evaluable (molecular profile group 367, standard group 197), early-stage high-intermediate risk, eight European countries, median age 69.0 years, median follow-up 58.1 months, randomised 2:1. The 367 women of the molecular profile group are drawn as a proportional bar in three parts: favourable 168 (46 per cent) observed with no adjuvant treatment at all; intermediate 148 (40 per cent) given vaginal brachytherapy, 21 Gy in 3 fractions; unfavourable 51 (14 per cent) given pelvic radiotherapy, 45.0 to 48.6 Gy. The primary endpoint, the 5-year cumulative incidence of vaginal recurrence, was 4.5 per cent (2.23 to 6.76) in the molecular profile group against 1.6 per cent (0.00 to 3.32) in the standard group, hazard ratio 2.71 (0.79 to 9.34); the upper bound of the one-sided confidence interval for the difference, 5.3 percentage points, lies below the pre-set non-inferiority margin of 7.0, p for non-inferiority = 0.005, drawn as a scale with the upper bound inside the margin and a note that non-inferiority proves the difference did not cross a line agreed in advance, not that the two are the same. In the favourable subgroup, the second primary analysis, 5-year vaginal recurrence was 4.1 per cent (0.81 to 7.37) against 0.9 per cent (0.00 to 2.78), hazard ratio 3.97 (0.48 to 32.95): the point estimate is fourfold, and it sits inside the margin only because the denominator is small and the interval so wide as to carry almost no information. A starred panel states that favourable is not the same as POLE mutant: in PORTEC-4a favourable means POLE mutant, or NSMP with wild-type CTNNB1, and the whole risk profile also takes in L1CAM overexpression and substantial lymphovascular space invasion, so reading it as "POLE mutation means no treatment" is wrong. Adverse events were mostly grade 1-2, with grade 3 or worse genitourinary toxicity in 4 of 367 (1 per cent) against 4 of 197 (2 per cent). The next block gives the four RAINBO colours, every row tagged "ongoing": p53abn-RED, for p53 abnormal, maintenance olaparib for 2 years after adjuvant chemoradiotherapy against chemoradiotherapy alone, planned 554, phase 3; MMRd-GREEN, radiotherapy with concurrent and adjuvant durvalumab for 1 year against radiotherapy alone, planned 316, phase 3; NSMP-ORANGE, for oestrogen-receptor-positive NSMP, a de-escalation of radiotherapy followed by 2 years of progestogen against chemoradiotherapy, planned 600, phase 3; and POLEmut-BLUE, a de-escalation with no adjuvant treatment, or none or radiotherapy alone for higher-risk patients, planned 145, phase 2. Beside them a timeline headed "timing: around 2030" gives December 2028 for the primary completion of RAINBO BLUE & TAPER (NCT05640999, 393 patients), January 2030 for the RAINBO umbrella trial (NCT05255653, estimated 1,615), and June 2030 for RAINBO-RED (NCT06712472, 554); a note records that the protocol paper expected main results from 2028 while the registry dates are later, so anyone deciding this year is still working from the post-hoc analyses above and one non-inferiority trial. At the foot of the figure a gold-bordered panel states that for most women with early-stage disease this does not change the treatment: in a prospective real-world study that put molecular classification into the multidisciplinary meeting, of 122 women after surgery with FIGO 2023 stage 1 to 2 disease the recommendation changed in only 25 (20.5 per cent), escalated in 15 (12.3 per cent) and de-escalated in 10 (8.2 per cent), the changes concentrated in the TP53-abnormal group (62.5 per cent against 10.2 per cent in the rest), with no NSMP or POLE mutant case changed - a single-institution study from India of 122 women covering only stage 1 to 2, so not strong evidence. The panel closes by saying that the figure shows direction rather than strength and that the strength of evidence differs from box to box - the PORTEC-3 molecular comparisons are post-hoc, PORTEC-4a proves non-inferiority, RAINBO has no results yet - and that whether anything is added or taken away is a conversation with the gynaecological oncology, radiation oncology and medical oncology teams. A further note records that fewer than 5 per cent have multiple classifiers, assigned in the order POLE mutant, then MMRd, then p53 abnormal.

en_alt: Schematic: four phase 3 immunotherapy trials, set out in two columns by MMR status, every cell carrying its MMR label and its n. The left column is mismatch repair deficient (dMMR/MSI-H), the right column mismatch repair proficient (pMMR/MSS), and each cell carries a hazard ratio plotted on a log scale with a dashed line at 1. First row, RUBY / ENGOT-EN6 / GOG-3031, first line for primary advanced (stage III/IV) or first recurrent disease, n=494 randomised, dostarlimab or placebo with carboplatin and paclitaxel. The dMMR/MSI-H cell, n=118 (23.9 per cent): 24-month progression-free survival 61.4 per cent (46.3 to 73.4) against 15.7 per cent (7.2 to 27.0), hazard ratio for progression-free survival 0.28 (0.16 to 0.50) and for overall survival 0.32 (0.17 to 0.63). The pMMR/MSS cell states that the subgroup size is not reported cell by cell (of the whole 494, 118 were dMMR/MSI-H): in the whole population, 24-month progression-free survival 36.1 per cent (29.3 to 42.9) against 18.1 per cent (13.0 to 23.9), hazard ratio 0.64 (0.51 to 0.80); and in pMMR/MSS the overall survival hazard ratio is 0.79 (0.60 to 1.04), the published wording being "a trend in favor of dostarlimab" - a trend, not an established survival benefit. Second row, NRG-GY018, first line, n=813, pembrolizumab or placebo with paclitaxel and carboplatin, patients split into two independent cohorts by MMR status. The dMMR cohort, n=225 (placebo 113, pembrolizumab 112): progression-free survival at 12 months 74 against 38 per cent, hazard ratio 0.30 (0.19 to 0.48); overall survival hazard ratio 0.55 (0.25 to 1.19), one-sided nominal P = 0.0617, not statistically significant and immature. The pMMR cohort, n=588 (295, 293): median progression-free survival 13.1 against 8.7 months, hazard ratio 0.54 (0.41 to 0.71); overall survival hazard ratio 0.79 (0.53 to 1.17), P = 0.1157, not significant. Third row, DUO-E / ENGOT-EN10 / GOG-3041, first line, three arms with randomisation stratified by MMR status, n=718. Both cells in this row carry an explicit hatched badge reading "subgroup size not obtainable": the dMMR and pMMR subgroup sizes could not be found in the available full text or in the trial registry results, so no number is given and none is invented. The dMMR subgroup: durvalumab against control, hazard ratio 0.42 (0.22 to 0.80), median progression-free survival not reached against 7.0 months; durvalumab plus olaparib against control 0.41 (0.21 to 0.75), median 31.8 against 7.0 months; and in this subgroup adding olaparib gave no further benefit over durvalumab alone (hazard ratio 0.97, 0.49 to 1.98). The pMMR subgroup: durvalumab 0.77 (0.60 to 0.97), median 9.9 against 9.7 months; durvalumab plus olaparib 0.57 (0.44 to 0.73), median 15.0 against 9.7 months; interim overall survival at about 28 per cent maturity, durvalumab 0.77 (0.56 to 1.07), P = 0.120, not significant, and durvalumab plus olaparib 0.59 (0.42 to 0.83), P = 0.003 - both whole-population figures. Fourth row, Study 309 / KEYNOTE-775, in women who have already had chemotherapy (at least one prior platinum regimen), n=827 (pMMR 697, dMMR 130), lenvatinib with pembrolizumab against chemotherapy of the physician's choice. dMMR, n=130: 5-year overall survival 36.5 against 9.8 per cent, 5-year progression-free survival 26.4 against 10.8 per cent, with no dMMR-specific hazard ratio reported for this cell. pMMR, n=697: median overall survival 17.4 against 12.0 months, hazard ratio 0.68 (0.56 to 0.84); median progression-free survival 6.6 against 3.8 months, hazard ratio 0.60 (0.50 to 0.72); 5-year overall survival 16.7 against 7.3 per cent. Below that row, a panel gives the cost: grade 3 or worse adverse events 88.9 against 72.7 per cent, and by five years (median follow-up 68.8 months) 32.3 against 5.9 per cent had stopped one of the drugs because of a treatment-related adverse event - a third of them did not get through the whole course. Next comes a red-bordered counter-example: ENGOT-en11 / GOG-3053 / KEYNOTE-B21, the adjuvant setting after curative surgery with no residual disease, n=1,095 randomised (pembrolizumab 545, placebo 550). The primary endpoint, disease-free survival in all patients, was not met: 119 events (22 per cent) against 121 (22 per cent), hazard ratio 1.02 (0.79 to 1.32), P = 0.570, 2-year disease-free survival 75 against 76 per cent; the interval is drawn clearly straddling 1. The pre-specified subgroups by MMR status are dMMR (n=281) 0.31 (0.14 to 0.69) and pMMR (n=814) 1.20 (0.91 to 1.57). A note records that the primary endpoint was not met and that the dMMR box is a subgroup analysis with few events and short follow-up, so it cannot be lifted out on its own as evidence that adjuvant immunotherapy works: working in advanced or recurrent disease is not the same as working when added after surgery. Below that, the single-arm data, the whole block labelled "single arm": KEYNOTE-158 (pembrolizumab alone, non-randomised open-label phase 2), previously treated advanced MSI-H/dMMR disease, efficacy population n=79, median follow-up 42.6 months, objective response rate 48 per cent (37 to 60), median progression-free survival 13.1 months, median overall survival not reached; and GARNET (dostarlimab alone, single-arm open-label phase 1), dMMR/MSI-H cohort n=129 with an objective response rate of 43.5 per cent (34.0 to 53.4) and MMRp/MSS cohort n=161 with 14.1 per cent (9.1 to 20.6). Single arm means there is nothing to compare against, and these response rates cannot be set beside the hazard ratios from the randomised trials above. The figure closes: every number has to be read together with its MMR status and its n; the four trials differ in setting, control arm, endpoint and length of follow-up, so reading across them does not work; and at the next appointment one thing should be settled first - has the MMR test been done, and is it deficient or proficient, because that line decides which column above is yours.

data, professional experience and consensus」，同一份文件也寫明到今天沒有隨機試驗比較過不同的藥物療法。中間是一條由 16 個關卡串成的鏈，從「起點：拿到切片報告」開始，每一格都帶指引自己給的等級，全部成立才通過：第一，類內膜腺癌、Grade 1、IA 期、沒有肌層侵犯、沒有風險因子（V, A）；第二，Grade 2 的證據 limited、只能個案討論（IV, C）；第三，請有經驗的病理專科醫師出第二意見（III, A）；第四，用 G1、G2、G3 三級制，不可以用二分法（III, A）；第五，診斷切片用子宮鏡導引，優於盲取（III, A）；第六，肌層侵犯用 MRI，或專門的放射科／超音波醫師做陰道超音波，且用標準化高品質協定（III, A）；第七，不可以用電腦斷層判肌層侵犯（III, A）；第八，用 MRI 或電腦斷層排除骨盆腔與主動脈旁淋巴結、遠端轉移（II, B）；第九，用骨盆 MRI 或陰道超音波排除附件侵犯（II, B）；第十，copy number high、也就是 p53 異常這型，保守治療並不適當（IV, D）；第十一，MMR 免疫染色是強制項目，用來抓 Lynch 高風險者（III, A）；第十二，完整 ProMisE 分類是鼓勵，但現有資料還不足以臨床應用（IV, B）；第十三，婦癌科、生殖醫學、病理科、放射科共同照護（V, A）；第十四，生殖潛能評估與生殖科諮詢要在治療開始之前完成（V, B）；第十五，治療期間體重控制 highly recommended（II, A）；第十六，Lynch 三句——確認有無其他癌、告知復發風險比其他人高、要不要做個案討論（II, A）。鏈的終點寫著：16 格全部成立，才輪到談藥怎麼用。鏈旁另有一格例外條款：若從子宮鏡切除下來的檢體懷疑有早期、局部的 1 到 2 公釐肌層侵犯，may be discussed on a case-by-case basis（IV, C），三個限定語一個都不能拿掉，它不是「有侵犯也可以留」。接著一格寫追蹤密度，標題是「有反應是要兩次切片才算數的事」：療程 6 到 12 個月內要達到完全反應（III, B），最長不超過 15 個月（IV, C）；6 個月完全沒有反應要進多專科諮詢（IV, B）；每 3 個月一次內診加超音波（IV, B），每 3 到 6 個月一次子宮鏡內膜組織評估（IV, B）；要間隔至少 3 個月的兩次連續切片都判完全反應才算成功（IV, C）。圖的下半是結果漏斗，資料來自收 46 篇、861 位臨床 IA 期、高分化類內膜病人的統合分析：完全反應 79.7%，分母是 861 人、46 篇；達到完全反應的人裡有 35.3% 在追蹤期間復發，分母是前一格達到完全反應的人；活產 20.5%，95% 信賴區間 15.7 到 25.8，分母是 650 人、39 篇。漏斗下方標明：這三個比例的分母不一樣，不可以把它們相乘；同一份統合分析另報懷孕率 26.7%（21.3 到 32.3；826 人、42 篇），只收 35 歲以下的次群活產率 30.7%，作者結論句是 only one-fifth of them are estimated to achieve live birth。再下面一格是完成生育之後：指引原文 Completion surgery is recommended after completing childbearing（II, A），理由句是 due to a high recurrence rate；治療沒有反應、懷不上、復發或惡化一樣建議手術（II, A）；生完後不想馬上開刀也不打算馬上懷第二胎的人，指引寫的是用含 levonorgestrel 的子宮內投藥系統做維持治療（III, B），那是延後不是取消。圖的最後是兩個方向的警語。左邊：這不是「吃藥就好」，也不是「反應了等於治好了」——它是在上面每一格都成立的前提下，用比較高的復發風險換一段生育時間，達到完全反應的人裡有 35.3% 復發。右邊：也不是「想生就不要肖想、直接切」——符合上面每一格的人是真的有機會，46 篇、861 人裡完全反應 79.7%、活產 20.5%，35 歲以下的次群 30.7%；條件符不符合是婦癌科、生殖醫學、病理科與放射科一起判的，不是自己對著文章判。
en_alt: Schematic of the entry gate and the outcome figures for fertility-sparing treatment of early endometrial cancer. At the top is a statement: every level on the page comes from the ESGO/ESHRE/ESGE 2023 fertility-sparing guideline, and of that guideline's 48 recommendations not one is Level I evidence, with only 16 reaching Level II; in its own words, "66% of the recommendations are supported only by observational data, professional experience and consensus", and the same document states that to date no randomised trial has compared the different types of medical treatment. The middle of the figure is a chain of 16 gates beginning at "the biopsy report in your hand", each carrying the level the guideline gave it, all of which have to hold. One: endometrioid carcinoma, Grade 1, Stage IA, without myometrial invasion and without risk factors (V, A). Two: evidence for Grade 2 is "limited", case-by-case discussion only (IV, C). Three: a second opinion from an experienced histopathologist (III, A). Four: use the G1/G2/G3 grading system, not the binary one (III, A). Five: hysteroscopic-guided biopsy is preferred over blind biopsy (III, A). Six: myometrial invasion assessed by MRI, or by transvaginal ultrasound from a specialised radiologist or sonographer, on standardised high-quality protocols (III, A). Seven: CT should not be used to assess myometrial invasion (III, A). Eight: MRI or CT to exclude pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes and distant metastases (II, B). Nine: adnexal involvement ruled out by pelvic MRI or transvaginal ultrasound (II, B). Ten: in copy-number-high, that is p53-abnormal, tumours conservative therapy would be inappropriate (IV, D). Eleven: mismatch repair immunohistochemistry is mandatory, to identify those at high risk of Lynch syndrome (III, A). Twelve: the full ProMisE classifier is encouraged, although available data do not allow clinical applicability (IV, B). Thirteen: joint care from gynaecological oncology, fertility medicine, pathology and radiology (V, A). Fourteen: reproductive potential assessed and fertility specialists consulted before treatment begins (V, B). Fifteen: weight control during treatment is highly recommended (II, A). Sixteen: the three Lynch lines — check for concurrent cancers, inform of the higher risk of persistence and recurrence, and discuss case by case (II, A). The chain ends with the note that all 16 have to hold before the drugs are even discussed. Beside it sits the exception clause: if an early and focal myometrial invasion of 1 to 2 mm is suspected from the resection material, a fertility-sparing approach may be discussed on a case-by-case basis (IV, C), and none of those three qualifiers can be dropped, because it does not mean that invasion can be left in place. A further panel, headed that "responding" is something two biopsies have to agree on, sets out the follow-up: a complete response should be achieved within 6 to 12 months (III, B) and in no more than 15 months (IV, C); in the absence of any kind of response at 6 months, multidisciplinary counselling is recommended (IV, B); clinical pelvic examination and ultrasound at every 3-month visit (IV, B) and endometrial histological assessment by hysteroscopy every 3 to 6 months (IV, B); and two consecutive biopsies at least 3 months apart both showing a complete response are needed before the treatment counts as successful (IV, C). The lower half is an outcome funnel from a meta-analysis of 46 studies and 861 women with clinical Stage IA, well-differentiated endometrioid carcinoma: complete response 79.7%, denominator 861 women in 46 studies; recurrence during follow-up in 35.3% of those who reached a complete response, denominator being that responding group; and live birth 20.5%, 95% confidence interval 15.7 to 25.8, denominator 650 women in 39 studies. A note states that the three proportions do not share a denominator and must not be multiplied together; that the same meta-analysis reports a pregnancy rate of 26.7% (21.3 to 32.3; 826 women, 42 studies) and a live birth rate of 30.7% in studies restricted to women aged 35 or under; and that the authors conclude "only one-fifth of them are estimated to achieve live birth". The next panel covers what happens after childbearing: "Completion surgery is recommended after completing childbearing" (II, A), with the reason given as "due to a high recurrence rate"; surgery is likewise recommended for non-responders, inability to conceive, recurrence or progression (II, A); and for women who decline surgery after delivery and are not planning a second pregnancy straight away, the guideline recommends maintenance with a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (III, B), which is a postponement and not a cancellation. The figure closes with two warnings in opposite directions. First, this is not "just take the drugs" and a response is not a cure: it works only while every cell above holds and trades a higher risk of recurrence for a window in which to conceive, with 35.3% of responders recurring. Second, nor is it "if you want a child, forget it — just operate": for women in whom every cell holds the chance is real, with a complete response in 79.7% and a live birth in 20.5% across 46 studies and 861 women, rising to 30.7% in studies of women aged 35 or under; and whether the conditions hold is judged jointly by gynaecological oncology, fertility medicine, pathology and radiology, not by a reader against an article.

en_alt: Schematic showing how the method of assessment decides the conclusion in lower-limb lymphoedema. The main title of the figure is "the method of assessment decides the conclusion". The upper half is four bars side by side, from a prospective study across 14 Swedish hospitals of 235 women, 116 of whom had a lymphadenectomy and 119 of whom did not, assessed before surgery and one year afterwards by all four methods in the same women, with both volume methods using a 10% increase as the threshold. For the same risk factor, lymphadenectomy, the adjusted odds ratios are: volume standardised for body mass index 14.42 (95% confidence interval 3.49 to 59.62); patient-reported 2.51 (1.33 to 4.73); clinical grading 2.11 (1.04 to 4.29); and raw volume calculated from limb circumference, where nothing shows at all, the result not reaching statistical significance. A dashed line marks an odds ratio of 1, meaning no difference detected. A note records that adjuvant radiotherapy behaves the same way: of these four methods only volume standardised for body mass index makes it come out as a risk factor (adjusted odds ratio 15.02, 95% confidence interval 2.34 to 96.57); and that the authors conclude "apparent risk factors for lymphedema differed considerably depending on the method used" and argue that the field needs an agreed gold-standard method. A further line warns that an odds ratio is not a multiple of a probability, that when an event is common an odds ratio looks much larger than the true multiple of risk, and that 14.42 therefore does not mean fourteen times the probability. The lower half labels the 1.3% to 49.4% range study by study with its method: Geppert 2018, clinical assessment, n=188 robotic surgery, 1.3% after sentinel lymph node mapping only against 18.1% after lymphadenectomy; Casarin 2025, questionnaire, n=239 laparoscopic surgery, 21.4% against 44.6%; Glaser 2021, a 13-item self-report questionnaire, n=378, 26.0% against 49.4%; and Leitao 2020, the same 13-item questionnaire, n=599, 27% against 41%. The adjusted odds ratios are Casarin 3.11, Glaser 2.75 and Leitao 1.8; and radiotherapy is a separate independent factor, with 51% of those who had external beam radiotherapy in the Leitao questionnaire reporting swelling against 35% of those who did not, an odds ratio of 1.95. A fifth study will not go on that axis at all: a Danish national prospective cohort of 486 women with low-grade, presumed stage I disease who all had sentinel lymph node mapping used the EORTC QLQ-EN24 leg lymphoedema score, from 0 to 100, before surgery and at 12 months, and the mean rise was 5.0 points (95% confidence interval 3.3 to 6.8), below the 8-point threshold for clinical significance; it reports a score rather than a percentage. The figure closes with two readings that are ruled out. First, this figure does not give you a probability: every number is tied to one method and one population, so averaging them or picking one treats a difference made by the method as a difference made by the body; nor does it mean that sentinel mapping prevents swelling, since 21.4% to 27% of the sentinel groups in the questionnaire studies still reported it. Second, self-massage cannot be written up as prevention: in the same Japanese cohort, 87 women who had no adjuvant treatment were grouped by preference, 24 performing simple lymphatic drainage daily for a year and 63 not, and over five years there was no difference in limb circumference change or in the extracellular-to-total water ratio, with a 5-year cumulative incidence of 37.5% against 23.5%, if anything the other way round; the authors state that "SLD does not contribute to the prevention of LLE".

en_alt: Schematic of the denominator behind recurrence in endometrial cancer and the salvage route for each site. The upper half is the denominator: among 2,815 women with FIGO 2009 stage I disease treated at two centres between 2009 and 2017, 278 recurred, that is 10%, and the other 90% did not. Splitting those 278, still as a proportion of all 2,815: isolated vaginal recurrence in only 61 women, 2% of the whole cohort, and recurrence outside the vagina in 217, 8% of the whole cohort. Three notes follow: of those 61 isolated vaginal recurrences, 42 or 69% were at the vaginal vault; among the 960 women who had adjuvant vaginal brachytherapy, 19 had an isolated vaginal recurrence, 2% again; and the median time to recurrence was 11 months for isolated vaginal recurrence against 20 months for recurrence elsewhere. The figure states that this set of numbers must be read in both directions: most women with stage I disease do not recur, and while the cell in which a vaginal vault recurrence can still be controlled is real, it is only 2% of stage I patients, so it is not what recurrence usually looks like but the most favourable kind of it. The lower half has four cells. First, isolated vaginal or vaginal vault recurrence with no previous radiotherapy: the population label is GOG-0238, n=165 randomised, the only randomised trial in this cell, with 82% low-grade, that is grade 1 or 2, endometrioid disease and the recurrence confined to the vagina in 86%. Progression-free survival at 3 years was 73% with radiotherapy alone against 62% with chemoradiotherapy, hazard ratio 1.25 (95% confidence interval 0.75 to 2.07); adding chemotherapy is a failed intervention in this setting, with no gain in progression-free survival and higher acute toxicity. The guideline recommends pelvic external beam radiotherapy plus intracavitary image-guided brachytherapy for vaginal vault recurrence (IV, A), with intracavitary image-guided brachytherapy alone an option for superficial tumours (IV, A). A single-centre series, Alban 2021, of 62 women with stage I to II disease and no previous adjuvant radiotherapy, reported vaginal control of 82% and overall survival of 61% at 5 years; but in that same series non-endometrioid histology carried a 12.5-fold risk of recurrence, and in a Japanese salvage brachytherapy series of 43 women, grade 1 to 2 against grade 3 at the original surgery gave 5-year overall survival of 96% against 40% and progression-free survival of 58% against 0%, so the 73% belongs to that particular population and cannot be lent to anyone else. Second, pelvic and lymph node recurrence: in PORTEC-1, as a historical comparison, survival 3 years after a pelvic recurrence was 8%, and the authors state plainly that survival did not differ between pelvic recurrence and distant metastasis. Pelvic exenteration is the heaviest option here: the COREPEX registry enrolled 862 women with gynaecological cancers and 676, or 78.4%, had tumour-free margins, with 5-year disease-free survival running from 43.7% down to 8.0% across four prognostic groups; the cost sits in the same cell, with severe early post-operative complications in 225 women or 26.1%, death within 30 days in 27 or 3.1% and severe late complications in 87 or 10.1%, and which group a woman falls into is decided by whether the margins can be clear and whether there is disease outside the pelvis. Third, an area that has already been irradiated: in PORTEC-1, again as a historical comparison, survival 3 years after a first recurrence was 51% in the control arm, which had not been irradiated, against 19% in the arm that had, P equals 0.004. The guideline recommends an external beam radiotherapy and image-guided brachytherapy boost after previous vaginal brachytherapy alone (IV, C); after previous external beam radiotherapy, the molecular subtype should be weighed in the decision about surgery or systemic treatment and radical surgery done only with clear margins, curative intent and acceptable morbidity (IV, A); and where surgery is not feasible, re-irradiation may be considered in experienced centres (IV, C). The re-irradiation denominators are all small: 22 women in Pittsburgh, with 3-year local control of 65.8% and overall survival of 68.1% and no grade 3 or higher bowel or bladder toxicity; and 32 women in Boston, with vaginal control of 64% at 3 years and 56% at 5 years and late grade 3 toxicity of 16% gastrointestinal, 13% urinary and 16% vaginal. Fourth, distant metastasis and disseminated recurrence: this cell carries no efficacy figures at all. The guideline defines oligometastatic disease as 1 to 5 lesions across no more than 3 sites, for which surgery, radical radiotherapy including stereotactic radiotherapy, or local ablation can be considered (IV, B); and first-line treatment of disseminated recurrence splits in two, both I, A, with chemotherapy plus an immune checkpoint inhibitor followed by maintenance for mismatch repair-deficient disease, and carboplatin with paclitaxel for the rest where disease is progressing quickly or causing symptoms. The cell shows only two arrows, pointing to the articles on who immunotherapy actually works for and on what adding chemotherapy buys and costs, where the figures live. Below the four cells a note records that everything marked as a historical comparison comes from PORTEC-1, a trial from the 1990s before image-guided brachytherapy existed, which can serve as a historical comparison but never as what to expect from treatment today. The figure closes with two warnings in opposite directions. First, a recurrence is not the end stage: for a low-grade, endometrioid recurrence confined to the vagina in someone not previously irradiated, the only randomised trial found 73% alive and free of progression at 3 years on radiotherapy alone, with chemotherapy added doing worse and costing more toxicity. Second, nor can every recurrence be brought back: survival 3 years after a pelvic recurrence was 8% and 19% for those already irradiated against 51% for those not, both historical comparisons; non-endometrioid histology carried a 12.5-fold risk of recurrence and grade 3 disease at the original surgery gave 0% progression-free survival at 5 years; and pelvic exenteration carries a 3.1% risk of death within 30 days. Every cell has its own denominator and they cannot be borrowed from one another.

D[S22] Klopp 2024（GOG-0238，n=165 隨機）——3 年無惡化存活單純放療 73% 對化放療 62%，HR 1.25（95% CI 0.75–2.07）；族群 82% 低惡性度（G1–2）類內膜、86% 復發侷限陰道；加化療未改善無惡化存活且急性毒性更高

D[S21] Creutzberg 2003（PORTEC-1，n=715；圖上一律標「1990 年代、無影像導引近接治療，只能當歷史對照」）——依部位分的 3 年存活只取骨盆復發 8% 一項（陰道 73%、遠端 14% 與 39/35/31/24 的救援鏈均未入圖，因為定稿正文沒有寫）；首次復發後 3 年存活：未照過放療 51% 對照過放療 19%（P=0.004）；作者結論句：骨盆復發與遠端轉移的存活沒有差別
D[S23] Alban 2021（n=62，第 1–2 期、先前未做輔助放療）——5 年陰道控制 82%、5 年整體存活 61%；非類內膜組織型復發風險 12.5 倍（P<0.01）
D[S26] Baek 2016（救援近接治療，n=43）——原發分化度 G1–2 對 G3 的 5 年整體存活 96% 對 40%、無惡化存活 58% 對 0%
D[S24] Ling 2019（再照射，n=22）——3 年局部控制 65.8%、3 年整體存活 68.1%，無 grade 3 以上腸道或膀胱毒性
D[S25] Lee 2022（再照射，n=32）——3 年與 5 年陰道控制 64% 與 56%；晚期 grade 3 毒性腸胃道 16%、泌尿道 13%、陰道 16%
D[S29]／D[S30] Bizzarri COREPEX（骨盆廓清術，20 家中心，n=862）——676 人（78.4%）切緣無腫瘤、依預後分數四組 5 年無疾病存活 43.7% 到 8.0%；嚴重早期術後併發症 225（26.1%）、30 天內死亡 27（3.1%）、嚴重晚期併發症 87（10.1%）

D[S1] ESGO-ESTRO-ESP 2025 指引原文——陰道頂端復發用骨盆外照射加腔內影像導引近接治療（IV, A）、表淺病灶可只做腔內影像導引近接治療（IV, A）；先前只做過陰道近接治療者加外照射與影像導引近接治療加強（IV, C）；做過骨盆外照射者將分子型納入根治性手術決定（IV, A）、手術不可行時有經驗中心可考慮再照射（IV, C）；寡轉移定義為 1–5 顆、分布最多 3 個部位（IV, B）；播散性復發第一線分 MMR 缺損與非 MMR 缺損兩條路（I, A）
